result:
I graded submission s1 for quiz 0001 and saved the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. Riley got 2 items correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | wrong (M4) | Riley picked "the model opens the booking system on its own". The model only writes a tool request, and the program runs the tool. |
| q3 | correct | A step limit is the safeguard against a stuck loop. |
| q4 | wrong (M4) | Riley answered 1 ("it runs the 3 tools itself"). The right answer is 4: three tool requests plus the final answer. |
| q5 | partial | "It sends it back to the model" is right, but it leaves out why: so the model can choose its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | partial (M3) | Choosing a tool from its description is right. The claim that the model remembers its tool choices across sessions on its own is wrong. |

**Summary:** Riley has the loop, the step limit and tool descriptions down. The idea to fix is who does what: the model only writes text, and the program runs the tools, calls the model again and does any remembering.

**Next step:** Riley should redo q2 and q4 by drawing the loop for "Is the laser cutter free tomorrow at 3 pm?" in two columns, "model writes" and "program does", and mark each model call.

I also added `learning-records/0003-who-runs-the-tools.md` for the open M4 and M3 misconceptions and updated `NOTES.md`. Submission s2, from four days later, is still ungraded. Do you want me to grade it next to see whether the misconceptions have been corrected?
